CITY OF PASADENA
  City Council Minutes
  September 29, 2022 - 5:00 P.M.
  City Hall Council Chamber

  SPECIAL MEETING
  The special meeting was convened and held virtually by videoconference/teleconference.

OPENING:  Mayor Gordo called the special meeting to order at 5:06 p.m. The
  pledge of allegiance was led by Councilmember Hampton.

ROLL CALL:  Mayor Victor M. Gordo
  Councilmembers:  Vice Mayor Andy Wilson
  Councilmember Tyron Hampton
  Councilmember Steve Madison
  Councilmember Gene Masuda
  Councilmember Jessica Rivas
  Councilmember Felicia Williams

  Staff:  City Manager Miguel Marquez
  City Attorney/City Prosecutor Michele Beal Bagneris
  City Clerk Mark Jomsky

  Mayor Gordo made introductory comments and provided an
  overview of the City Council District 3 interview and appointment
  selection process.

  The following members of the City Council publicly disclosed for the
  record their relationship, interaction and/or encounters with the
  three applicants, Justin Jones, Brandon Lamar, and Lucious Smith:

  Mayor Gordo stated that he has known Pastor Lucious Smith for
  approximately 30 years, and was with him at the hospital the day
  Councilmember Kennedy passed away. He also reported on brief
  candid conversations with all three applicants regarding their
  interest in applying to fill the District 3 Council vacancy. Mayor
  Gordo noted that he saw Justin Jones at the Playhouse Village Park
  opening but they did not discuss the application process.

  Councilmember Rivas stated that Mr. Lamar reached out to her
  before the application period had opened and prior to the ad hoc
  committee's decision to not meet with applicants. She reported that
  they had a brief and broad discussion about the application process
  in general and her experience going through the process in 2021
  as one of the applicants for the District 5 vacancy.

  Councilmember Williams stated that she is familiar with Justin
  Jones from his work on the Environmental Advisory Commission,
  and noted the two had spoken over the summer regarding some
  environmental policies and priorities. She also reported that she
  spoke with Mr. Jones regarding her experience on the City Council,

Council Minutes  09/29/2022
   before there was any restrictions regarding Councilmembers
  speaking with applicants about the appointment, as well as
  speaking with Brandon Lamar at the Playhouse Village Park
  opening and with Pastor Smith today in the hallway of City Hall.

  Councilmember Madison stated that he also knows Pastor Smith,
  whose church is in his district, and considers him a friend. He noted
  that he recently saw Pastor Smith at a memorial vigil honoring
  Councilmember Kennedy in front of City Hall. Councilmember
  Madison reported that Pastor Smith left him a voicemail but did not
  return the call since it was agreed not to meet with the applicants
  outside the public interview process.

  Councilmember Hampton stated that he knowns all three
  applicants. He reported that he attended the same memorial vigil
  for Councilmember Kennedy in front of City Hall, as well as funeral
  services for the late District 3 representative, which Pastor Smith
  also attended. Councilmember Hampton reported that he returned
  a phone call from Pastor Smith call, but let him know that the ad
  hoc committee agreed not to meet with applicants outside the public
  interview process. Councilmember Hampton reported that Mr.
  Jones is his appointee to the Environmental Advisory Committee,
  and that he spoke with Brandon Lamar after the ad hoc committee
  convened, to talk about some of Mr. Lamar's work with the Human
  Services Commission. He reported that he had not discussed the
  application process with any of the applicants.

  Councilmember Masuda and Vice Mayor Wilson stated that they
  had no direct interaction with the any of the three applicants.

  Mark Jomsky, City Clerk, reported that the City Clerk's Office
  received twenty-nine letters in support of Justin Jones, eighty-nine
  letters in support of Brandon Lamar, one letter in support of Lucious
  Smith, and fifteen letters providing comments on the appointment
  process, qualities for the City Council to consider when making the
  appointment, noting the pressing concerns in District 3; and/or
  advocating for a City Charter amendment to allow for a special
  election in lieu of an appointment process; with all correspondence
  distributed to the City Council, posted on-line, and made part of the
  public record.

PUBLIC COMMENT  The following individuals provided comments and concerns with the

AGENDA  Daniel Gonzalez, Pasadena resident
  Yadi, Pasadena resident

Council Minutes  2  09/29/2022
   The following individuals advocated for the City Council to appoint
  Brandon Lamar as Pasadena Council District 3 Councilmember:

  Tina Fredericks, Pasadena resident
  Kimberly Douglas, Pasadena resident
  Kaveh Naeeni, Pasadena resident
  Dawn Burkhardt, Pasadena resident
  Aeryn Levey, Pasadena resident
  Brigitte Rooney, Pasadena resident
  Ashay Patel, Pasadena resident
  Ed Washatka, Pasadena resident
  Maria Skelton, Van Nuys resident
  Miss Bernard, Pasadena resident

  APPLICANT PRESENTATIONS, INTERVIEWS, AND CITY
  COUNCIL SELECTION OF AN APPOINTEE TO FILL A
  VACANCY ON THE CITY COUNCIL, REPRESENTING DISTRICT
  3, PURSUANT TO CITY CHARTER SECTION 404

  The Mayor thanked the public speakers and individuals who
  submitted correspondence for their participation; and reported that
  applicants will be interviewed in the following order (as was
  determined by random drawing): Lucious Smith, Brandon Lamar,
  and Justin Jones.

  Lucious Smith, Brandon Lamar, and Justin Jones, District 3
  applicants, individually participated in an interview process,
  provided an overview of their personal and professional
  experiences, and responded to questions asked by each member
  of the City Council.

  Following all presentations/interviews, the City Council deliberated
  on the qualifications of each applicant for the District 3 vacancy; and
  expressed their thanks, appreciation, and gratitude to all three
  applicants for their willingness and interest to serve in this important
  role to represent District 3.

  Mayor Gordo, Vice Mayor Wilson, Councilmembers Hampton,
  Masuda and Williams expressed their support for Justin Jones.

  Councilmembers Madison and Rivas expressed their support for
  Brandon Lamar.

  Following discussion, it was moved by Councilmember Hampton,
  seconded by Councilmember Williams, to nominate Justin Jones to
  serve as the appointed City Councilmember representing District 3:

  AYES:  Councilmembers Hampton, Masuda, Williams, Vice
  Mayor Wilson, Mayor Gordo
  NOES:  Councilmember Rivas

Council Minutes  3  09/29/2022
   ABSENT: None
  ABSTAIN: Councilmember Madison

I  The City Council congratulated and welcomed Justin Jones as the
  newly appointed Pasadena City Councilmember for District 3.

  OATH OF OFFICE ADMINISTERED TO NEWLY APPOINTED
  DISTRICT 3 COUNCILMEMBER BY CITY CLERK

  City Clerk Jomsky administered the oath of office to Justin Jones
  as Pasadena City Councilmember representing District 3.

  Mr. Jones thanked the City Council and the community for the
  opportunity to serve the residents of District 3.

  ADJOURNMENT  On order of the Mayor, the special meeting of the City Council
  adjour ed at 9:30 p.m.
